# Upstream Wren's test suite, on the ESP32-C6

Generated by `tools/report-tests.py` from a run of `tools/run-tests.py`.
**Do not edit by hand** — the next run overwrites it.

This is upstream's own suite, unmodified, driven over the serial console
against `ports/esp32c6-wren`. Every test is sent whole between `.run` and
`.end` and scored against the `// expect:` comments the file already
carries, so "passes the suite" means here what it means upstream.

It exists for two reasons. It says how much of Wren actually works on this
part, which is not a given — and it is the yardstick the Rust
implementation will be held to, one group at a time.

| | |
|---|---|
| board | ESP32-C6FH4 rev v0.2 @ 160 MHz |
| port | ports/esp32c6-wren |
| wren | vendor/wren 0.4.0, unmodified |
| run | 2026-09-19 00:28:20 UTC |

## What a failure here means

A failure is one of three things, and the pages below say which:

* **Wren does not support it on this part** — a real limitation, and the
  most interesting outcome.
* **The harness cannot express it** — `api/` tests call into C, and
  `// stdin:` tests need input this console does not feed.
* **The board ran out of something** — memory or time. Those show as
  timeouts and are a footprint finding rather than a correctness one.


## Known failures

25 of the language suite does not pass. They are not
equivalent, and lumping them into one number would hide the only
ones that say something about Wren.

### A real limit of this part (2)

The most interesting outcome: Wren does something here that this hardware cannot survive. These are the numbers the Rust implementation is measured against, and they should **not** be made to pass.

| test | why |
|---|---|
| `language/deeply_nested_gc.wren` | reboots the board -- deep GC nesting exhausts the stack |
| `language/many_reallocations.wren` | reboots the board -- exhausts the heap |

### This console cannot express the test (7)

Not Wren's problem. A test that needs more source than the board has memory for, or a facility this port does not provide.

| test | why |
|---|---|
| `language/module/relative_import/relative_import.wren` | needs a resolveModuleFn: nested `./x` is relative to the importer, and the registry is keyed on the literal string |
| `language/variable/too_many_locals.wren` | needs more source than the console can carry to hit the limit |
| `limit/many_constants.wren` | the source is 513 KB; the board has 512 KB of RAM in total |
| `limit/many_globals.wren` | the source is 1.5 MB; three times the board's entire RAM |
| `limit/reuse_constants.wren` | the source is 513 KB; the board has 512 KB of RAM in total |
| `limit/too_many_constants.wren` | needs the 513 KB source above to reach the limit it tests |
| `meta/get_module_variables.wren` | inspects a module by name; the console registers modules under the import string, not a resolved path |
